title: Model the thinking, not the answer
statement: A worked example shows the reasoning, not just the answer: it thinks aloud where to look and why each tempting wrong choice is rejected, never making the thinking look easy.
detail: The reading project's lesson-structure rulings say the modelling step must show thinking, why this detail and not that one and what was rejected and why, and never just reveal a filled-in organiser; one ruling likened a reveal-only model to copying a neighbour's work. A July 2026 review of the rebuilt course asked the same: the model should show that choosing the relevant detail is hard when the text offers several, and sound like an adult explaining their thinking, not a drill of questions. The worked example works on the source in view, weighs the tempting wrong choice and other plausible options, and rejects each for a reason that does not apply as well to the answer it keeps.
against: Another file from the same review counts the move in 3 of 18 lessons, not 1 (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/course-red-team/references/finding-taxonomy.md`, line 191).
